answer: Each agent identity can join a market only after its controller locks a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond. Trades build a reputation tied to that bond; proven fraud forfeits it, while honest participants recover it after the dispute window. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and lock a separate token for every fake identity, tying up capital and risking its loss for as long as the fakes operate. A harbor, willow, or garden can host agents, but none makes identities free.
